title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the set-up of diagram (32) on p.750 and completes the sentence begun there.

The data are as follows.
- M is a profinite 'LT-group'.
- Π ⊂ M is a closed normal subgroup carrying an 'L-structure'. This seems to mean a profinite surface-type group with its inertia/peripheral data and a cyclotomic character, 'roughly Π = SL(2,Z)^'.
- Π0 is a discrete 'discretification' of Π, so Π = closure of Π0.
- G0 is a discrete group containing and normalizing Π0.
- G is the closure of G0 in M, assumed normal in M.

The page states the following.
1. G is a quotient of the profinite completion of G0, but for the moment it is not required to be isomorphic to that completion.
2. The same holds for τ = G/Π and τ0 = G0/Π0. The marginal note 'Donc = G0/Π0' defines τ0. The machine transcription wrongly reads these as Γ, Γ0.
3. Interpretation of the pieces:
   - τ0 plays the role of a 'discrete' Teichmüller group (mapping class group);
   - τ plays the role of a profinite completion of the Teichmüller group;
   - Γ = M/G plays the role of a profinite Galois group.
   So one has exact sequences 1→Π→G→τ→1 and 1→G→M→Γ→1, with a discrete skeleton 1→Π0→G0→τ0→1.
4. Two extreme cases are singled out.
   - Case (a): G0 = Π0, hence G = Π and τ trivial. This comes from a smooth relative multiplicity (stack) over a field finitely generated over Q, or more generally a scheme or multiplicity of finite type over Q. Π is the geometric (relative) fundamental group and M the arithmetic one. This is the classical anabelian situation 1→π1^geom→π1→Gal→1.
   - Case (b): G0/Π0 is isomorphic to the Teichmüller group of Π0, i.e. the mapping class group seen as the orientation-preserving outer automorphisms of the surface group, or to a finite-index subgroup of it. Here the 'modular' situation is the main interest.
5. The next page spells out case (b).
   - Π is the fundamental group of a suitable modular multiplicity (M_{g,n}).
   - T is its geometric part and T0 its transcendental (discrete) part.
   - Γ is Gal(Q̄/Q).
   Concretely, G0 can be taken as the mapping class group Γ_{g,n+1} acting on the fibre surface group Π0 = π_{g,n} via the Birman sequence. G is then the geometric π1 of the universal curve and M its arithmetic π1.

Purpose: an axiomatic, group-theoretic packaging of 'Galois–Teichmüller' situations. On the next page it serves to study homomorphisms M → G(A_Q) (adelic points of an algebraic group with a character) satisfying compatibility conditions. These include a strengthened condition (3° forte) of compatibility with the discrete Teichmüller group.
errors: No mathematical error on the page. The claim that G is a quotient of the profinite completion of G0 is correct, since G is the closure of the image of G0.
'Π ≈ SL(2,Z)^' is only heuristic. SL(2,Z)^ is virtually free profinite, not a surface group; Grothendieck himself says 'à peu près'.

Grothendieck explicitly leaves open whether G ≅ (G0)^, τ ≅ (τ0)^ and Γ0 completions agree. In case (b) this is the congruence-subgroup-type question for mapping class groups (the equality of the 'complétifié' and the profinite completion). It is a genuine gap he is aware of, not an error.

ideas.what: Axiomatic diagram (32): profinite tower Π ⊂ G ⊂ M with discrete skeleton Π0 ⊂ G0, quotients τ0 (discrete Teichmüller), τ (completed Teichmüller), Γ = M/G (Galois)
ideas.modern_name: Outer Galois representations on profinite surface groups / Grothendieck–Teichmüller set-up; cf. Mochizuki–Hoshi 'outer representations of PSC/NN type'
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, Longue Marche), developed by Ihara, Drinfeld, Nakamura, Matsumoto, Lochak–Schneps, Hoshi–Mochizuki
ideas.where_published: The general philosophy is in Esquisse d'un programme and the transcribed parts of La Longue Marche. This 'LT-structure' axiomatization does not appear in what I know to be published.

ideas.what: Case (a): G0 = Π0, arithmetic vs geometric π1 of a smooth multiplicity of finite type over Q
ideas.where_published: SGA1 Exp. IX–X; letter to Faltings; Esquisse

ideas.what: Case (b): G0/Π0 = (finite-index subgroup of) the Teichmüller group of Π0; modular interpretation via M_{g,n} and the Birman exact sequence, with Γ = Gal(Q̄/Q)
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on profinite mapping class groups / Teichmüller tower; Birman sequence and its profinite completion
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §2–3; La Longue Marche (Teichmüller tower)

ideas.what: Distinguishing the closure-completion ('complétifié') from the full profinite completion of the discrete group
ideas.modern_name: Congruence subgroup problem for mapping class groups; goodness / exactness of completed Birman sequence
ideas.where_published: Implicit in Esquisse remarks on the Teichmüller tower; not stated as such

missed.claim: An abstract axiomatic framework of 'LT-groups' with L-structured normal subgroup and discrete skeleton is used to unify the anabelian case (a) and the modular Teichmüller case (b). On the next page it serves to study homomorphisms M → G(A_Q) compatible with the discrete Teichmüller group. This axiomatization and its intended use (adelic representations of arithmetic Teichmüller groups) were not developed in the literature in this form.
missed.quote: Le groupe τ0 joue le rôle d'un groupe de Teichmüller "discret", le groupe τ celui d'un complétifié de gr. de Teichmüller, le groupe Γ = M/G joue le rôle d'un groupe de Galois profini.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is close in spirit to Hoshi–Mochizuki's combinatorial anabelian 'outer representations' and to Boggi–Lochak work on profinite Teichmüller groups. The coupling with adelic algebraic groups (next page) hints at a motivic/automorphic programme not explicitly pursued. It is of mainly historical interest unless the later pages develop it.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a clear unpublished axiomatic formulation of the Galois–Teichmüller set-up, distinguishing discrete and completed Teichmüller groups and anabelian versus modular extremes. Its content is philosophically consistent with the Esquisse and later GT literature. The novelty is in the formal packaging, not in a new result.
transcription_corrections: 'idem pour Γ et Γ0' should read 'idem pour τ et τ0'. The marginal '= G0/Π0' defines τ0 (cf. diagram (32): τ over Π→G^, τ0 under Π0→G0).
'Le groupe Γ0 joue le rôle' should read 'Le groupe τ0 joue le rôle'; 'le groupe Γ celui d'un complétifié' should read 'le groupe τ celui d'un complétifié'.
Line 2 likely reads 'isomorphe à ce complétifié lui-même' rather than 'complétifié bien-[?]'.
In case a), 'Π est' / 'N est en fait' is struck out; the surviving text says Π is 'le groupe fondamental relatif de la dite multiplicité'.
In case b), the line should read 'G0/Π0 ≃ groupe de Teichmüller de Π0, ou d'indice fini dans ce gr. de T. — dans ce cas, on est intéressé surtout à une situation "modulaire", où'.
